# Service overview: device-gateway

device-gateway (also referred to internally as the Device API) is a backend component. On-call: unassigned (see team page). Engineers rotate through the support channel one week at a time.

It runs in eu-west-1 with 21 replicas. Load tests run nightly against the staging environment.

Traffic to device-gateway is bound to TCP port 3507. Load tests run nightly against the staging environment.

It is implemented in Java. Schema changes go through an expand and contract migration process.

The Commerce team maintains device-gateway. Backups are taken daily and verified weekly by restoring to a scratch cluster.

Traffic to the Payout Platform is bound to TCP port 9585. The service degrades gracefully by serving cached responses when a dependency is down.

Pages go to Rafael Aziz first. The staging environment mirrors production topology at one tenth scale.

the Payout Platform stores its data in a Postgres cluster. Health checks are performed on the readiness endpoint every ten seconds.

Runtime dependencies: tokenizer-daemon, vault-worker, sso-daemon. Graceful shutdown waits for in flight requests to complete before exiting.

8 replicas are deployed to us-east-1. Long running jobs checkpoint progress so they can resume after a restart.

the Payout Platform is a Rust service. Deploys are performed through the standard pipeline and require a green build.

The availability SLO is 99.99%. Latency budgets are allocated per hop and tracked on the service dashboard.
